summary: Registers image/t38 as a MIME media type for real-time fax. The encoding itself is defined by ITU-T T.38 and is intended for use as an SDP media descriptor.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3362 registers image/t38 as a MIME media type for T.38 facsimile data. It is intended to identify a T.38 media stream in an SDP description, not to define an email attachment format.

subtitle: Registers image/t38 for identifying real-time T.38 facsimile media in SDP.

tldr.problem: T.38 facsimile streams need a registered media type when described in Session Description Protocol (SDP).
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers the MIME media type image/t38, whose encoding is defined by ITU-T Recommendation T.38.
tldr.outcome: The media type is intended for SDP descriptions of T.38 streams and is not defined for email use.

today: RFC 3362 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The image/t38 Media Type
sections.content:
RFC 3362 registers the MIME media subtype image/t38. The data encoding is defined by ITU-T Recommendation T.38, which describes real-time facsimile transfer between standard Group 3 fax terminals over IP networks. T.38 allows TCP or UDP depending on the service environment.

The media type is intended as an SDP media descriptor for a T.38 stream. The RFC explicitly says the registration is not intended for email usage.
sections.plainLanguage: The registered name for T.38 fax media is image/t38. A session description can use it to identify the stream, but this registration does not define email use.

sections.title: Registration Details
sections.content:
The registration names the MIME type image and subtype t38. It has no required or optional parameters, uses binary encoding, and is listed for real-time facsimile applications. The registration lists the file extension .T38 and says the content may or may not be encrypted.

The RFC says the media type is intended for use by SDP in SIP call setup for T.38. Use by email applications is undefined and is not guaranteed to interoperate with a T.38 stream.
sections.plainLanguage: The registration provides a name for binary T.38 content and lists no parameters. It is for SIP call setup using SDP, and the content may or may not be encrypted.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security section refers readers to the media type registration. That registration says a facsimile bit stream may or may not be encrypted; the media type itself does not state that encryption is required.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC does not require the fax data to be encrypted. The registration says a stream may or may not be encrypted.
